items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: He turned out to be my dearest friend.

ctx.x: Well, and sure enough you are.

And listen to this. Ben Webster got on late. And I must have weighed about 109 pounds soaking wet. And Ben Webster staggered to the men’s room and me standing there being introduced to the band, and he said, “Now who is that?” He said, “What is that” talking about me. And Cab say, “That’s the new bass player.” He said, “A new what?” And I said I’d never like him as long as I lived. He turned out to be my dearest friend.
Yeah, he was fun guy. He was always putting people on, making people think he was a cad, but he wasn’t, he was really a good guy.

items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: To my dying day he‟s my dearest friend.

ctx.x: A little bit because in intermission we played pinochle and he put a big light behind him and he put the cards up like this. He put them all in place and he didn‟t look at them again. You just say ten of Jack, ten of spades and if he had the jack, he‟d put the jack on it. But I‟m working and Cab Calloway is making his first trip with [Unintelligible] to California where Al Jolson, the same kid from the movie… Ben Webster‟s in Cab Calloway‟s band. He‟s got this great band and a fabulous bass player, Al Morgan,…
